docs.title: MCP Context Provider
docs.text:
Persistent tool context + learned instincts for Claude – eliminate context loss between sessions.

The MCP Context Provider is a context and instinct engine for Claude Desktop and Claude Code. Instead of re-explaining your preferred rules, naming conventions, and syntax preferences in every session, the server automatically injects them - available in all sessions without manual effort.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Contexts (static): Tool-specific rules in JSON, always injected at full confidence
  • Instincts (learned): Compact rules distilled from sessions, confidence-scored, human-approved
  • Auto-corrections: Syntax transformations run automatically (e.g. Markdown to DokuWiki)
  • Memory Bridge: Syncs instincts and contexts to mcp-memory-service for persistence across machines

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/doobidoo/MCP-Context-Provider.git
cd MCP-Context-Provider
npm install && npm run build
npm link   # recommended: makes mcp-cp and mcp-context-provider available globally

Add to your global Claude Code config (~/.claude.json) or Claude Desktop config:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "context-provider": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/path/to/MCP-Context-Provider/dist/server/index.js"],
      "env": {
        "CONTEXTS_PATH": "/path/to/MCP-Context-Provider/contexts",
        "INSTINCTS_PATH": "/path/to/MCP-Context-Provider/instincts"
      }
    }
  }
}

Global installation is recommended - the context provider works across all projects. See Installation for full instructions.

docs.title: Version
docs.text: v2 is in beta. See the Changelog for the latest release.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Session Start
  → Engine loads Contexts (JSON) + Instincts (YAML)
  → MCP Server exposes its tools (stdio or HTTP)
  → Claude queries tools for context injection

docs.title: MCP Tools
docs.text: Tool Description get_tool_context Get complete context for a tool category get_syntax_rules Get syntax-specific rules list_available_contexts List all loaded contexts apply_auto_corrections Apply correction patterns to text build_injection Combined context + instinct injection payload list_instincts List instincts with confidence scores, plus the resolved store path store_instinct Store a new instinct candidate (inactive until approved) approve_instinct Approve an instinct for active use reject_instinct Deactivate an instinct and lower its confidence record_outcome Record a positive, negative, or neutral outcome for an instinct sync_instincts Push all local instincts to the memory service (requires the memory bridge) sync_contexts Push all loaded contexts to the memory service restore_contexts Pull contexts from the memory service into CONTEXTS_PATH

docs.text:

docs.title: The /instill Skill
docs.text:
/instill analyzes your Claude Code session and extracts instincts - compact, reusable rules that prevent you from repeating the same corrections across sessions.

Example: You keep telling Claude "don't use em-dash". After running /instill, it captures this as an instinct that automatically triggers whenever Claude writes text.

Install globally (one-time setup; the symlink stays current with git pull):

mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/instill
ln -s /path/to/MCP-Context-Provider/.claude/skills/instill.md ~/.claude/skills/instill/SKILL.md

Then use /instill in any session. Manage saved instincts with the CLI:

mcp-cp list                        # List all instincts with confidence scores
mcp-cp approve <id>                # Human approval (required for activation)
mcp-cp tune <id> --confidence 0.8  # Adjust confidence
mcp-cp path                        # Print the resolved store directory

See Installation - The /instill Skill for details.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to the MCP Context Provider project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Context sync to the memory service (#7): sync_contexts pushes every loaded context into mcp-memory-service, restore_contexts pulls them back and writes them into CONTEXTS_PATH. This existed in the v1.8 Python line and was dropped in the TypeScript rewrite. One memory per context: a one-line summary as the searchable content, the exact file text in metadata.payload — measured to round-trip byte for byte, where storing the file as memory content does not (the service splits it into overlapping chunks and returns one of them). Existing files are never overwritten without force, which keeps a .bak. A context opts out with metadata.sync: false, and contexts in subdirectories of CONTEXTS_PATH are never loaded and so never pushed. The round trip holds for contexts within the memory service's Cloudflare metadata limit; a context over that limit is refused at push time rather than silently dropped (see Fixed, below).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A second sync of unchanged content deleted the remote copy: a push replaces a memory by deleting it and storing the same content again. The memory service hashes content only, and since 12.4.0 it refuses to re-create content it has a delete on record for unless the client sends restore_deleted: true. The bridge never sent it, so the store came back 409 right after the delete had gone through: the instinct or context was gone from the service and every later push failed the same way. Both store calls now send the flag. Content deleted on the service side therefore returns on the next push, which is what a push from the local files means.
  • The project .mcp.json pointed the bridge at a port nothing listens on: it had http://127.0.0.1:8001/api, while the memory service defaults to port 8000 and so does DEFAULT_BRIDGE_CONFIG. The file now defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8000/api and takes MEMORY_BRIDGE_URL from the environment when it is set, so a local instance on HTTPS or another port needs no edit to a tracked file. The doc comment on MemoryBridgeConfig.baseUrl said 8001 as well.
  • A restore did not reach the running engine: Engine.initialize() runs once at startup and nothing watches the contexts directory, so after restore_contexts wrote a file the engine kept serving — and pushing back — the text it had read before. On a second machine, a restore_contexts --force followed by a sync_contexts in the same session pushed the older local text over the newer remote copy, inverting what the feature promises. A pull that actually wrote something now re-reads the contexts directory, so both the injected contexts and the files sync_contexts pushes reflect what is on disk.
  • A conflict did not say what conflicted: the design has restore_contexts report an existing file as a conflict "showing the local and remote context_version", but ContextWriter skipped it with a bare "file exists" and never read the version it already had in hand. The skip reason now names both — the remote version from the memory, the local one read from the file on disk, each falling back to unknown when it is missing or the local file is not parseable.
  • A pulled context's identity was never cross-checked: ContextWriter validated the payload against the schema but never compared the tool_category inside it with the category the memory was stored under, and the no-overwrite guard is keyed on the file name while the engine keys a context by tool_category. A memory carrying any fresh, valid file_name was therefore written without force and then injected into sessions as instructions under whatever category it declared inside. A payload whose tool_category does not match the recorded category is now refused, with both values in the reason.
  • Two contexts declaring the same tool_category collided silently: ContextLoader.loadAll keys its map by category, so the second file to load simply replaced the first, with directory order deciding the winner and nothing said about it. The collision is now reported in errors, naming both files. Which file wins is unchanged.
  • A service that ignored paging hung the session: ContextSync.pullFromMemory left its loop only on a short page, so a service answering every request with a full page looped without end, growing an array, inside an MCP tool call. The pull now stops after MAX_PULL_PAGES (20) full pages — 1000 contexts at the page size it uses, against a store that holds tens — and throws rather than returning a truncated set that would look complete to the writer.
  • A failed list call looked like an empty store: HttpMemoryBridge.listContexts returned { memories: [], total: 0 } on any non-OK response, and the pull loop reads an empty page as "no more contexts". A 500 on the first page made restore_contexts report "nothing to restore"; a 500 on page three of five silently returned a partial set. It now throws with the HTTP status, the way storeContext already did, and the restore_contexts handler surfaces that as a tool error.
  • A rejected memory store looked like a success: the memory service can answer a /memories POST with HTTP 200 and { success: false, content_hash: null } — for example when its own semantic-duplicate detection rejects the content — and HttpMemoryBridge.storeContext/storeInstinct checked only the HTTP status, so sync_contexts and sync_instincts reported the item as pushed while nothing was stored. Found while verifying sync_contexts end to end against the live service: two synthetic contexts with near-identical summaries triggered the service's dedup and one push silently vanished. The response body is now checked for success and a string content_hash; a rejection now surfaces through the existing per-item errors list instead of being counted as pushed.
  • A context over the Cloudflare metadata limit synced without error and then vanished: the memory service's Cloudflare tier enforces a flat 10KB cap on memory metadata (CLOUDFLARE_MAX_METADATA_SIZE_KB), but only on the background sync from local storage to the durable tier — the initial write still succeeds. Four contexts in this repository are over that line (dokuwiki 10.0KB, anti_ai_voice 13.9KB, n8n 18.4KB, azure 23.0KB): sync_contexts reported them pushed, they landed in local storage, and were then silently dropped before reaching Cloudflare. ContextSync.pushToMemory now measures the metadata it is about to send — including the context_category and source keys the bridge appends before serializing, which count against the limit too — the way the service itself measures it: as Python's json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=True) would encode it, where every non-ASCII code point costs 6 bytes (12 for one outside the Basic Multilingual Plane) rather than its raw UTF-8 byte count. A first pass at this fix measured raw UTF-8 bytes and both undercounted non-ASCII-heavy metadata and missed those two appended keys — a context under the real cap by raw byte count could still be over it once escaped, the same silent-drop shape as the original bug, just for a narrower band of inputs; no context in this repository is in that band today. A context over the limit is now refused before anything is sent (default 9500 bytes, a margin under the service's flat cap — not a value taken from the service itself), reporting the actual size and the limit in errors instead. The limit is a constructor option, so a deployment without the Cloudflare tier can raise or disable it. Chunking oversized metadata is out of scope here.
  • A failed lookup let a push leave the old copy behind: a push finds the memory it is about to replace by tag, deletes it and stores the new one. HttpMemoryBridge.searchByTags answered a failed search with an empty list, which reads as "nothing to replace": the store went through and, once the summary had changed, the old copy stayed next to the new one, for restore_contexts to pick up. It now throws with the HTTP status, and the push reports that item as an error and stores nothing. This applies to sync_instincts as well.
  • A custom context tag made every push miss its previous copy: the bridge stores and lists contexts under contextTag from its config, but ContextSync searched with the literal context-json. The lookup now goes through findContexts on the bridge, which uses the configured tag.
  • A push accepted file names a restore refuses: the loader takes any *_context.json, the writer only lowercase basenames. MyProject_context.json was reported as pushed and could never be written back. Such a name is now refused at push time with the rule in the error.
  • A restore replaced an existing file it could not read: ContextWriter treated every failed read as "file missing", so a context that existed but was unreadable was overwritten without force and without a .bak. Only ENOENT counts as missing now; any other read error skips the item and says why.
  • Two overlapping restores could overwrite each other: both saw the target missing and both renamed into place, and within one process they shared a temp file name. An unforced write now links the temp file into place, which fails if the target appeared in the meantime, and temp names are random.
  • A restore into a directory that did not exist yet wrote nothing: on a new machine with a fresh CONTEXTS_PATH every write failed with ENOENT. The directory is now created.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The instinct store has exactly one source: the engine and the CLI read learned.instincts.yaml and nothing else. Previously every *.instincts.yaml in the store directory was merged together, which made "which file is this instinct in" unanswerable and let a second file drift in unnoticed. Any other instinct file in the directory is now reported by name at startup and by mcp-cp list, together with the mcp-cp import command that merges it — present and visible, never silently mixed in.
  • mcp-cp import always writes to the canonical file; the --into <name> flag is gone, because importing into any other name produced a file the engine would never read.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A test passed locally and failed in CI: the durability test for an unreadable store used chmod 000, which root ignores. Woodpecker runs the suite as root in a node:20 container, so the read succeeded there, append() did not throw, and the test failed — while passing for any normal user. It now puts a directory where the store file belongs, which fails with EISDIR for every uid.
  • A store that could not be parsed was silently replaced by an empty one: InstinctLoader.append() and the store_instinct handler both fell back to {version, instincts: {}} on any load failure and then saved that over the existing file. One transient parse failure was enough to discard a whole store — a 232-instinct store was wiped down to a single entry this way. Loading now falls back to an empty file only on ENOENT; an existing file that cannot be read or parsed raises an error naming the file instead of overwriting it.
  • Writes are atomic: InstinctLoader.save() writes to a temporary file and renames it into place, so an interrupted or concurrent write can no longer leave a half-written store on disk for the next load to choke on.
  • The whole pipeline failed to compile: the validate-json step's one-liner contained echo "Checking: $(basename $f)", and YAML read the : inside it as a mapping separator, so the command parsed as a map instead of a string. Every run — push and pull request alike — ended as error before a single step executed. Rewritten as a block scalar. This had been latent since the step was written; nothing ran it until the repository was enabled at ci.codeberg.org.
  • The Woodpecker UI's "Run pipeline" button did nothing: manual was missing from the top-level event filter, so a hand-triggered run was skipped in full — the same class of defect as the missing tag event, and just as silent. Added.
  • License metadata contradicted the LICENSE file: package.json, both .claude-plugin manifests, mkdocs.yml and the README/docs license sections all said MIT, while LICENSE has been Apache-2.0 since the initial commit. The LICENSE file is the operative grant, so the metadata was corrected to Apache-2.0. This is not a relicensing — it aligns the metadata with the licence that was always in effect.
  • Woodpecker never ran on tags: the top-level when: event: [push, pull_request] gated the whole pipeline, so a tag event started nothing and the release step's own when: event: tag was unreachable. tag is now part of the top-level filter, so a release tag runs the same gates as a push.
  • The release step promised more than it did: it re-ran npm ci, npm run build and npm test — the same gates as the steps above it — and created no release and published no package. Removed. The Codeberg release is created via the Forgejo API by the release manager, and npm publish stays manual until a registry token exists as a Woodpecker secret. CLAUDE.md and the release-manager agent described the pipeline as "test to build to release" and have been corrected.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Instincts store no longer depends on the launch directory (#1): the default was ./instincts resolved against whatever CWD the MCP host started the server from, so the store silently split per launch directory — four disjoint stores had accumulated with zero overlap between them, and instincts had landed in unrelated repositories. Resolution is now INSTINCTS_PATH → ./instincts only when the CWD is an mcp-context-provider checkout → $XDG_DATA_HOME/mcp-context-provider/instincts → ~/.local/share/mcp-context-provider/instincts.
  • Contexts path had the same CWD dependency: CONTEXTS_PATH → ./contexts when in a checkout → the contexts/ directory shipped with the package. Contexts are versioned with the code, so the packaged directory is the correct fallback.
  • Server and CLI could operate on different stores: both now resolve through src/config/paths.ts. mcp-cp no longer defaults to ./instincts.
  • Loader rejected files whose instincts: key held a list instead of a map keyed by id — a shape some /instill runs produced. It is now normalized like the legacy top-level array form, and a missing or unknown version is defaulted to "1.0" instead of failing the schema literal.
  • Server version was hardcoded (2.0.0-alpha.6 while the package was at 2.0.0-beta.1) and is now read from package.json.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:

  • mcp-cp path: print the resolved store directory and which rule produced it.
  • Startup path logging: both resolved paths go to stderr at startup, and the server warns when the store sits inside a git working tree that is not this repository's checkout — the signal that a CWD was picked up by accident.
  • list_instincts now returns store: { path, resolved_from }, and the HTTP /health payload reports both paths plus the server version. A store you cannot locate from inside a session is a store you cannot trust.

docs.title: Fixed

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Auto-repair loader (src/engine/instinct-loader.ts): The loader now detects and auto-corrects three classes of damage at the system boundary:
  • Shape normalization: top-level array → canonical {version, instincts} object
  • ID synthesis: entries without id get a kebab-case slug generated from the first 4 words of their rule text
  • Collision resolution: duplicate ids are suffixed numerically (foo → foo-2)
  • Repair reporting: every fix is tracked in a RepairAction[] report returned alongside the parsed file. New methods: loadWithRepairs(), repair(). The repair() method persists canonical form back to disk with a .bak copy of the original.
  • Engine auto-repair integration: Engine.initialize() now collects repairs per file and, when autoRepair: true, persists corrections to disk. New accessor getFileRepairs().
  • MCP_CP_AUTO_REPAIR environment variable: enables persistent repair mode in the server (default: 1). Set to 0 to keep initialize() side-effect free (in-memory corrections only).
  • 8 regression tests (src/__tests__/instinct-loader.test.ts): canonical load, array normalization, id synthesis, collision resolution, entries too short to slug, content-validation-after-repair, persistent repair with .bak handling, no-op repair on clean files.

docs.text: The Context Provider ships with three memory-related contexts covering different layers of the memory ecosystem.

docs.title: memory_context.json – MCP Memory Auto-Trigger
docs.text:
Category: memory Purpose: Proactive storage and retrieval rules for the MCP Memory Service. Defines when Claude should automatically store memories and when to proactively retrieve them based on conversation patterns.

Session Initialization: On startup, loads recent activity (last 24h) and retrieves any open tasks tagged in-progress, active, or follow-up.

Auto-Store Triggers — Claude stores a memory when it detects:

Trigger Example Patterns Tags Applied Decisions "I decided to", "We agreed that", "Let's go with" decision, {project} Technical solutions "The fix was", "The solution is", "To resolve this" solution, technical Completed activities "I completed", "I implemented", "I resolved" activity, completed Future tasks "I need to", "TODO:", "Remember to" todo, in-progress Preferences "I prefer", "I always", "My preference is" preference, personal Learning moments "I learned that", "It turns out", "The issue was" learning, insight

Auto-Retrieve Triggers — Claude retrieves memories when it detects:

  • Temporal queries: "What did I do last week", "Yesterday", "Earlier today"
  • Continuation: "Continue with", "Where were we", "Pick up where"
  • Problem solving: "How did I fix", "What was the solution for"

Smart Tagging: Automatically detects project names, tool names (Terraform, Docker, Azure, Git, Python, etc.), and adds temporal tags (day, month, year).

docs.title: python_mcp_memory_context.json – MCP Memory Service Development
docs.text:
Category: python-mcp-memory Purpose: Specialized context for developing and extending the MCP Memory Service itself. Provides FastAPI patterns, MCP protocol conventions, storage backend configurations, and Cloudflare integration rules. Activate this when working on the mcp-memory-service codebase.

Session Initialization: Loads last 7 days of MCP Memory Service development activity, retrieves architecture and backend config context, and surfaces any open mcp-memory-service tasks.

Auto-Store Triggers:

Trigger Example Patterns Tags Applied MCP protocol changes "tool handler", "JSON-RPC", "stdio transport" mcp-protocol, mcp-memory-service Storage backend config "Cloudflare backend", "SQLite-vec", "Vectorize index" storage-backend, configuration Cloudflare setup "CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN", "Workers AI", "D1 setup" cloudflare, setup Hybrid backend "dual storage", "background sync", "graceful fallback" hybrid-backend, sync FastAPI implementation "API endpoint", "async route", "SSE events" fastapi, api Troubleshooting solutions "fixed by", "root cause", "resolved by" troubleshooting, solution

Auto-Retrieve Triggers:

  • Backend errors → searches cloudflare, storage-backend, troubleshooting
  • MCP connection issues → searches mcp-protocol, connection
  • Async errors → searches async, troubleshooting, python
  • Performance issues → searches performance, optimization

Code Style Rules:

# Type hints required, async preferred, Python 3.10+
async def handle_store_memory(arguments: dict) -> list[TextContent]:
    ...

Preferences: uv as package manager, pytest for tests, black formatter, ruff linter, Google docstrings, 80% minimum test coverage.

docs.title: shodh_memory_context.json – SHODH Episodic Memory
docs.text:
Category: memory Purpose: Context rules for the SHODH Cloudflare Memory backend — a separate memory system focused on episodic memory with emotional metadata, credibility scoring, and associative retrieval. Used as the backend for the SecondBrain app.

Key Differentiators vs. memory_context.json:

  • Episodic grouping: Related memories are grouped into episodes (30min timeout)
  • Emotional metadata: Auto-detects valence/arousal from conversation patterns (joy, frustration, satisfaction, concern)
  • Credibility scoring: Each memory gets a credibility score (user-stated=1.0, ai-generated=0.7, inferred=0.5)
  • Typed memories: Observation, Decision, Learning, Error, Discovery, Pattern, Context, Task

Memory Types:

Type When Used Decision "decided to", "we agreed", "going with" Learning "I learned", "lesson learned", "key insight" Error "fixed the", "resolved by", "workaround is" Discovery "I discovered", "it turns out", "TIL" Pattern "best practice", "always do", "rule of thumb" Task "TODO:", "don't forget", "action item" Context "working on", "focusing on", "today's goal" Observation "I noticed", "worth noting"

Proactive Context: Calls proactive_context on every message with a surface threshold of 0.65 — memories are surfaced automatically without explicit retrieval requests.

docs.text: Complete reference for creating and configuring context files in the MCP Context Provider.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Context files are JSON documents that define tool-specific rules, preferences, and automatic corrections. Each file represents a category of tools and their associated context rules.

docs.title: Basic Template
docs.text:
{
  "tool_category": "string",
  "description": "string", 
  "auto_convert": boolean,
  "syntax_rules": {},
  "preferences": {},
  "auto_corrections": {},
  "metadata": {}
}

docs.title: tool_category (required)
docs.text:
• Type: String
  • Description: Identifier for the tool category
  • Examples: "dokuwiki", "terraform", "azure", "git"
  • Usage: Used to match tool names and apply appropriate context

docs.title: description (required)
docs.text:
• Type: String
  • Description: Human-readable description of the context
  • Example: "DokuWiki-specific context rules and syntax preferences"

docs.title: auto_convert (optional)
docs.text:
• Type: Boolean
  • Default: false
  • Description: Whether to automatically apply corrections when tools are used
  • Example: true

docs.title: syntax_rules (optional)
docs.text:
Defines formatting and syntax conversion rules.

{
  "syntax_rules": {
    "headers": {
      "format": "====== {} ======",
      "levels": {
        "1": "====== {} ======",
        "2": "===== {} ====="

def validate_context_file(file_path: Path) -> bool:
    """Validate context file structure and content"""
    try:
        with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
            context = json.load(f)

        # Required fields
        required_fields = ['tool_category', 'description']
        for field in required_fields:
            if field not in context:
                print(f"Missing required field: {field}")
                return False

        # Validate auto_corrections regex patterns
        auto_corrections = context.get('auto_corrections', {})
        for name, rule in auto_corrections.items():
            if 'pattern' in rule:
                try:
                    re.compile(rule['pattern'])
                except re.error as e:
                    print(f"Invalid regex pattern in {name}: {e}")
                    return False

        return True

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error validating context file: {e}")
        return False

docs.title: Quick Start Guide
docs.text: Get the MCP Context Provider running in 5 minutes with this step-by-step guide.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The MCP Context Provider gives Claude persistent memory across chat sessions. Instead of losing context when you restart Claude Desktop, your tool preferences, syntax rules, and best practices persist automatically.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.8+ (check with python --version)
  • Claude Desktop installed and working
  • Internet connection for downloading dependencies

docs.title: 🚀 Option 1: Automated Installation (Recommended)
docs.text:
For Linux/macOS/Unix: 

# One-line install
curl -sSL https://codeberg.org/doobidoo/MCP-Context-Provider/raw/branch/main/install.sh | bash

For Windows: 

# Download and run installer
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://codeberg.org/doobidoo/MCP-Context-Provider/raw/branch/main/install.bat" -OutFile "install.bat"
.\install.bat

What it does: - ✅ Downloads the MCP Context Provider package - ✅ Creates a Python virtual environment - ✅ Installs all dependencies - ✅ Configures Claude Desktop automatically - ✅ Verifies the installation

Skip to Step 4 if using automated installation.

docs.title: Step 1: Install Prerequisites
docs.text:
Install DXT CLI: 

npm install -g @anthropic-ai/dxt

Verify installation: 

dxt --version
python --version  # Should be 3.8+

docs.title: Step 2: Download and Extract
docs.text:
# Download the DXT package
wget https://codeberg.org/doobidoo/MCP-Context-Provider/raw/branch/main/mcp-context-provider-1.2.1.dxt

# Extract to your preferred location
dxt unpack mcp-context-provider-1.2.1.dxt ~/mcp-context-provider
cd ~/mcp-context-provider

docs.title: Step 3: Set Up Python Environment
docs.text:
# Create virtual environment
python -m venv venv

# Activate it
source venv/bin/activate  # Linux/macOS
# OR
venv\Scripts\activate     # Windows

# Install dependencies
pip install mcp>=1.9.4

docs.title: Step 4: Configure Claude Desktop
docs.text:
Find your configuration file: - Linux: ~/.config/claude/claude_desktop_config.json - macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json - Windows: %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json

Add this configuration: 

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "context-provider": {
      "command": "/home/user/mcp-context-provider/venv/bin/python",
      "args": ["/home/user/mcp-context-provider/server/context_provider_server.py"],
      "env": {
        "CONTEXT_CONFIG_DIR": "/home/user/mcp-context-provider/contexts",
        "AUTO_LOAD_CONTEXTS": "true"
      }
    }
  }
}

Important: Replace /home/user/mcp-context-provider with your actual installation path.

docs.title: Step 5: Verify Installation
docs.text:
Run the verification script: 

cd ~/mcp-context-provider
python verify_install.py

Expected output: 

✓ Python version: 3.11.5
✓ MCP package installed
✓ Contexts directory found
✓ Found 5 JSON files
✓ Server loads successfully (5 contexts)
=== Installation verified ===

docs.title: Step 6: Restart and Test
docs.text:
1. Restart Claude Desktop completely
  2. Start a new chat in Claude Desktop
  3. Test the installation by asking Claude:
Can you list available contexts using the MCP Context Provider?

Expected response: Claude should use the list_available_contexts tool and show: - dokuwiki - terraform - azure - git - general_preferences

    optimizations = []

    # 1. Reduce memory query frequency
    if session_time > 0.1:
        optimizations.append("Reduce memory query frequency in session initialization")
        performance_report['optimizations_applied'].append("memory_query_optimization")

    # 2. Cache effectiveness scores
    if any(t > 0.05 for t in analysis_times):
        optimizations.append("Implement effectiveness score caching")
        performance_report['optimizations_applied'].append("effectiveness_caching")

    # 3. Batch memory operations
    optimizations.append("Batch memory operations for better performance")
    performance_report['optimizations_applied'].append("batch_operations")

    # Store performance optimization recommendations
    await provider.memory_service.store_memory(
        f"Performance optimization analysis: {len(optimizations)} optimizations recommended",
        ["performance", "optimization", "analysis"],
        performance_report
    )

    print("Performance Optimization Report:")
    print(f"  Baseline Total Time: {baseline_time:.4f}s")
    print(f"  Session Init Time: {session_time:.4f}s")
    print(f"  Average Analysis Time: {performance_report['baseline_metrics']['average_analysis_time']:.4f}s")
    print(f"  Optimizations Recommended: {len(optimizations)}")

    for opt in optimizations:

# Optimize performance

docs.title: The /instill Skill
docs.text: /instill is a Claude Code skill that extracts learned rules (instincts) from your current session. When you notice Claude making the same mistakes, or you keep correcting the same patterns, /instill captures those as reusable instincts.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Analyzes your session for repeated corrections, explicit preferences, workflow patterns
  2. Extracts candidates as compact rules (20-80 tokens each)
  3. Presents them for review with an interactive prompt:
## Instinct Candidates (3 found)

### 1. `no-em-dash`
> domain: writing | confidence: 0.7

**Rule:** "Never use em-dash (—). Use colon, comma, semicolon, or rephrase."
**Triggers:** `—`, `em-dash`

### 2. `terraform-snake-case`
> domain: terraform | confidence: 0.8

**Rule:** "All Terraform resource names must use snake_case, never camelCase."
**Triggers:** `resource`, `terraform`

**Reply with:** a (accept all) | 1,2 (accept specific) | e1 (edit) | r (reject all)
  1. Saves accepted instincts to learned.instincts.yaml in the resolved store (mcp-cp path prints it)
  2. Instincts are automatically injected in future sessions when their trigger patterns match

docs.title: Install globally
docs.text:
The skill must be installed as a global Claude Code skill to work across all projects:

mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/instill
ln -s /path/to/MCP-Context-Provider/.claude/skills/instill.md ~/.claude/skills/instill/SKILL.md

The symlink keeps the skill current with git pull.

Skill directory structure

Global skills require the path ~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md — a flat file like ~/.claude/skills/instill.md will not be recognized.

After installation, /instill is available in every Claude Code session. Type /instill to extract instincts, or /instill git to focus on a specific domain.

docs.title: Optional: Memory Bridge
docs.text:
Connect to mcp-memory-service to keep instincts and contexts across machines:

{
  "env": {
    "MEMORY_BRIDGE_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api",
    "MEMORY_BRIDGE_API_KEY": "your-api-key"
  }
}

With the bridge configured:

  • sync_instincts pushes the local instincts.
  • sync_contexts pushes every loaded context, one memory per context. A context with metadata.sync: false is skipped, and contexts in subdirectories of CONTEXTS_PATH are never loaded and so never pushed.
  • restore_contexts pulls contexts back and writes them into CONTEXTS_PATH. Existing files are left untouched and reported; force: true overwrites and keeps a .bak.

A context whose metadata is over the 9500-byte sync limit is refused at push time, with the size named in the error.

From mcp-memory-service 12.4.0 on, the service refuses to re-create content it has a delete on record for unless asked. The bridge sends restore_deleted: true with every store, so syncing unchanged content twice keeps one memory per item. Verified for contexts against 12.10.0.

If the service runs on HTTPS with a certificate from a private CA (mkcert, for example), set NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS to the CA file in the same env block.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Variable Default Description CONTEXTS_PATH packaged contexts/ Path to *_context.json files INSTINCTS_PATH ~/.local/share/mcp-context-provider/instincts Directory holding learned.instincts.yaml MEMORY_BRIDGE_URL (none) Memory service base URL (enables bridge) MEMORY_BRIDGE_API_KEY (none) API key for memory service MCP_SERVER_PORT 3100 HTTP server port (only with --http) MCP_CP_AUTO_REPAIR 1 Write a repaired instinct file back to disk (a .bak is kept). Set to 0 to repair in memory only

Both paths are optional overrides. Without INSTINCTS_PATH the store resolves to ./instincts only inside an mcp-context-provider checkout, then $XDG_DATA_HOME/mcp-context-provider/instincts, then the default above. If you set them, use absolute paths.

docs.title: Migration from v1.x
docs.text:
v2.0 is a complete rewrite from Python to TypeScript. Key changes:

v1.x (Python) v2.x (TypeScript) python context_provider_server.py node dist/server/index.js CONTEXT_CONFIG_DIR CONTEXTS_PATH AUTO_LOAD_CONTEXTS Always auto-loads DXT packaging npm install 4 MCP tools Context tools plus instinct lifecycle tools No instincts Instinct engine with confidence scoring stdio only stdio + HTTP transport

Context JSON files (contexts/*_context.json) are compatible. The v2 Zod schema is stricter:

  • auto_corrections values must be {pattern, replacement} objects (not plain strings)
  • session_initialization requires enabled (boolean) and actions fields

docs.title: Context Sync Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Push context files into mcp-memory-service and write them back onto another machine, byte for byte.

Architecture: One memory per context. The exact file text lives in metadata.payload, so it round-trips without chunking; content is a one-line summary so the context stays findable by semantic search. A new ContextSync mirrors the existing InstinctSync, and a separate ContextWriter owns every disk write because that is where path traversal and overwrite risk live.

Tech Stack: TypeScript (ESM, NodeNext), Zod, vitest, Node built-in fetch. No new dependencies.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-02-context-sync-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Node >=20. ESM only: every relative import ends in .js, including from .ts sources.
  • Zero new runtime dependencies.
  • npm run lint is tsc --noEmit and must stay clean; the repo compiles under strict with noUncheckedIndexedAccess, so index access needs ! or a guard.
  • Tests are vitest with globals: false — import describe, it, expect explicitly from vitest.
  • No emoji in code, comments, commit messages or docs.
  • Commit messages: Conventional Commits, imperative subject, no AI/assistant attribution and no Co-Authored-By for tooling.
  • Marker tag for contexts: context-json. Per-context tag: context:<tool_category>. Also tag portable.
  • Payload metadata keys are payload, file_name, context_version, content_sha256, source, synced_at. Never chunk_index, total_chunks or original_hash — those belong to the memory service's own auto-splitting.
  • Valid context file name: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*_context\.json$, basename only.
  • Never overwrite a context file without an explicit force, and keep a .bak when forcing.
  • All file writes go through temp-file-then-rename, matching InstinctLoader.save().

// src/__tests__/helpers/fake-memory-bridge.ts
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import type {
  IMemoryBridge,
  MemoryRecord,
  MemorySearchResult,
} from '../../bridge/types.js';

/**
 * In-memory IMemoryBridge for tests. Stores whole records so a test can
 * assert on tags and metadata, and counts stores so a re-push can be checked
 * for duplication.
 */
export class FakeMemoryBridge implements IMemoryBridge {
  readonly records = new Map<string, MemoryRecord>();
  storeCalls = 0;
  healthy = true;

  async healthCheck(): Promise<boolean> {
    return this.healthy;
  }

  private put(content: string, tags: string[], type: string, metadata: Record<string, unknown>): string {
    const hash = createHash('sha256')
      .update(content + JSON.stringify(tags) + String(this.storeCalls))
      .digest('hex');
    const now = Date.now() / 1000;
    this.records.set(hash, {
      content,
      content_hash: hash,
      tags,
      memory_type: type,
      metadata,
      created_at: now,
      created_at_iso: new Date(now * 1000).toISOString(),
      updated_at: null,
      updated_at_iso: null,
    });
    this.storeCalls += 1;
    return hash;
  }

  private byTags(tags: string[], matchAll: boolean): MemoryRecord[] {
    return [...this.records.values()].filter((r) =>
      matchAll ? tags.every((t) => r.tags.includes(t)) : tags.some((t) => r.tags.includes(t)),
    );
  }

  async storeInstinct(
    instinctId: string,
    content: string,
    tags: string[],
    metadata: Record<string, unknown>,
  ): Promise<string> {
    return this.put(content, ['instinct', `instinct-id:${instinctId}`, ...tags], 'instinct', metadata);
  }

  async storeContext(
    category: string,
    content: string,
    tags: string[],
    metadata: Record<string, unknown>,
  ): Promise<string> {
    return this.put(
      content,
      ['context-json', `context:${category}`, ...tags],
      'context',
      { ...metadata, context_category: category, source: 'mcp-context-provider' },
    );
  }

  async searchInstincts(_query: string, _limit = 5): Promise<MemorySearchResult[]> {
    return [];
  }

  async searchByTags(
    tags: string[],
    matchAll = false,
    marker = 'instinct',
  ): Promise<MemorySearchResult[]> {
    return this.byTags([marker, ...tags], matchAll).map((memory) => ({
      memory,
      similarity_score: 1,
      relevance_reason: 'tag match',
    }));
  }

  async deleteInstinct(contentHash: string): Promise<boolean> {
    return this.records.delete(contentHash);
  }

  async deleteContext(contentHash: string): Promise<boolean> {
    return this.records.delete(contentHash);
  }

  async listInstincts(page = 1, pageSize = 50): Promise<{ memories: MemoryRecord[]; total: number }> {
    return this.page(this.byTags(['instinct'], true), page, pageSize);
  }

  async listContexts(page = 1, pageSize = 50): Promise<{ memories: MemoryRecord[]; total: number }> {
    return this.page(this.byTags(['context-json'], true), page, pageSize);
  }

  private page(
    all: MemoryRecord[],
    page: number,
    pageSize: number,
  ): { memories: MemoryRecord[]; total: number } {
    const start = (page - 1) * pageSize;
    return { memories: all.slice(start, start + pageSize), total: all.length };
  }
}

// src/__tests__/context-sync.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach } from 'vitest';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { ContextSync } from '../bridge/context-sync.js';
import { FakeMemoryBridge } from './helpers/fake-memory-bridge.js';
import type { Context, LoadedContextFile } from '../types/context.js';

let bridge: FakeMemoryBridge;
let sync: ContextSync;

function context(category: string, sync?: boolean): Context {
  return {
    tool_category: category,
    description: `${category} rules`,
    auto_convert: false,
    metadata: {
      version: '1.2.0',
      applies_to_tools: [`${category}:*`],
      ...(sync === undefined ? {} : { sync }),
    },
  };
}

function loaded(category: string, syncFlag?: boolean): LoadedContextFile {
  const ctx = context(category, syncFlag);
  return {
    fileName: `${category}_context.json`,
    raw: JSON.stringify(ctx, null, 2) + '\n',
    context: ctx,
  };
}

beforeEach(() => {
  bridge = new FakeMemoryBridge();
  sync = new ContextSync(bridge);
});

describe('ContextSync.pushToMemory', () => {
  it('stores the exact raw text in metadata.payload', async () => {
    const file = loaded('git');
    const result = await sync.pushToMemory([file]);

    expect(result.pushed).toEqual(['git']);
    const record = [...bridge.records.values()][0]!;
    expect(record.metadata['payload']).toBe(file.raw);
    expect(record.metadata['file_name']).toBe('git_context.json');
    expect(record.metadata['context_version']).toBe('1.2.0');
    expect(record.metadata['content_sha256']).toBe(
      createHash('sha256').update(file.raw).digest('hex'),
    );
  });

  it('puts a one-line summary in content, not the payload', async () => {
    await sync.pushToMemory([loaded('git')]);

    const record = [...bridge.records.values()][0]!;
    expect(record.content).toBe('Context git: git rules');
    expect(record.content).not.toContain('applies_to_tools');
  });

  it('tags the memory with the marker and the category', async () => {
    await sync.pushToMemory([loaded('git')]);

    const record = [...bridge.records.values()][0]!;
    expect(record.tags).toContain('context-json');
    expect(record.tags).toContain('context:git');
    expect(record.tags).toContain('portable');
  });

  it('replaces rather than duplicates on a re-push', async () => {
    await sync.pushToMemory([loaded('git')]);
    await sync.pushToMemory([loaded('git')]);

    expect(bridge.records.size).toBe(1);
    expect(bridge.storeCalls).toBe(2);

  it('skips a context with metadata.sync false', async () => {

    expect(result.skipped).toEqual([
      { category: 'git', reason: 'metadata.sync is false' },

// src/bridge/context-sync.ts
/**
 * Bidirectional sync of context files with mcp-memory-service.
 *
 * One memory per context. `content` is a one-line summary so the context
 * stays findable by semantic search; the exact file text lives in
 * `metadata.payload`, which round-trips byte for byte. Storing the file as
 * memory content does not round-trip: the service splits content over its
 * backend limit into overlapping chunks and returns one of them.
 *
 * This class never touches the filesystem. Writing pulled contexts to disk
 * is ContextWriter's job.
 */

import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import type { Context, LoadedContextFile } from '../types/context.js';
import type { IMemoryBridge } from './types.js';

export const CONTEXT_MARKER_TAG = 'context-json';

export interface ContextPushResult {
  /** Categories stored. */
  pushed: string[];
  /** Categories deliberately not stored, with the reason. */
  skipped: Array<{ category: string; reason: string }>;
  /** Categories whose store failed. */
  errors: Array<{ category: string; error: string }>;
}

/** The single line that gets embedded, and therefore searched. */
export function contextSummary(context: Context): string {
  return `Context ${context.tool_category}: ${context.description}`;
}

export function sha256(text: string): string {
  return createHash('sha256').update(text).digest('hex');
}

export class ContextSync {
  constructor(private readonly bridge: IMemoryBridge) {}

  /**
   * Push contexts into the memory service, replacing any earlier copy of the
   * same category. Idempotent: a re-push leaves one memory per context.
   */
  async pushToMemory(files: LoadedContextFile[]): Promise<ContextPushResult> {
    const result: ContextPushResult = { pushed: [], skipped: [], errors: [] };

    for (const file of files) {
      const category = file.context.tool_category;

      if (file.context.metadata.sync === false) {
        result.skipped.push({ category, reason: 'metadata.sync is false' });
        continue;
      }

      try {
        const existing = await this.bridge.searchByTags(
          [`context:${category}`],
          true,
          CONTEXT_MARKER_TAG,
        );
        for (const match of existing) {
          await this.bridge.deleteContext(match.memory.content_hash);
        }

        await this.bridge.storeContext(
          category,
          contextSummary(file.context),
          ['portable'],
          {
            payload: file.raw,
            file_name: file.fileName,
            context_version: file.context.metadata.version,
            content_sha256: sha256(file.raw),
            synced_at: new Date().toISOString(),
          },
        );

        result.pushed.push(category);
      } catch (e) {
        result.errors.push({
          category,
          error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e),
        });
      }
    }

    return result;
  }
}

  /**
   * Read every context memory. Returns payloads with their recorded file
   * name and an integrity verdict; writing them is the caller's decision.
   */
  async pullFromMemory(): Promise<PulledContext[]> {
    const pulled: PulledContext[] = [];
    const pageSize = 50;
    let page = 1;

    for (;;) {
      const { memories, total } = await this.bridge.listContexts(page, pageSize);
      if (memories.length === 0) break;

      for (const memory of memories) {
        const payload = memory.metadata['payload'];
        const fileName = memory.metadata['file_name'];
        if (typeof payload !== 'string' || typeof fileName !== 'string') continue;

        const category =
          typeof memory.metadata['context_category'] === 'string'
            ? memory.metadata['context_category']
            : '';
        const version =
          typeof memory.metadata['context_version'] === 'string'
            ? memory.metadata['context_version']
            : '';
        const expected = memory.metadata['content_sha256'];

        pulled.push({
          category,
          fileName,
          version,
          payload,
          integrityOk: typeof expected === 'string' && sha256(payload) === expected,
        });
      }

      if (page * pageSize >= total) break;
      page += 1;
    }

    return pulled;
  }

// src/bridge/context-writer.ts
/**
 * Writes pulled contexts to disk. The only place in the codebase that does.
 *
 * The file name arrives from the memory service, which makes it untrusted
 * input to a filesystem write. It is validated as a basename, and the
 * resolved target is checked to still sit inside the contexts directory,
 * before anything is written. A `file_name` of "../../.ssh/authorized_keys"
 * must not be a way out of that directory, whatever put it there.
 *
 * Writes are atomic (temp file, then rename) and never silent: an existing
 * file is left alone unless `force` is set, and forcing keeps a `.bak`.
 */

import { copyFile, readFile, rename, unlink, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { join, resolve, sep } from 'node:path';
import { ContextSchema } from '../schema/context.schema.js';
import type { PulledContext } from './context-sync.js';

/** Context file names this writer accepts. Basename only, lowercase. */
export const VALID_CONTEXT_FILENAME = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*_context\.json$/;

export interface ContextWriteResult {
  /** File names written. */
  written: string[];
  /** File names not written, with the reason. */
  skipped: Array<{ fileName: string; reason: string }>;
}

export class ContextWriter {
  constructor(private readonly contextsPath: string) {}

  async write(
    pulled: PulledContext[],
    options: { force?: boolean } = {},
  ): Promise<ContextWriteResult> {
    const result: ContextWriteResult = { written: [], skipped: [] };
    const force = options.force === true;

    for (const item of pulled) {
      const skip = (reason: string): void => {
        result.skipped.push({ fileName: item.fileName, reason });
      };

      if (!VALID_CONTEXT_FILENAME.test(item.fileName)) {
        skip('invalid file name');
        continue;
      }

      const target = resolve(this.contextsPath, item.fileName);
      if (!target.startsWith(resolve(this.contextsPath) + sep)) {
        // Belt and braces: the regex already rules out separators.
        skip('invalid file name');
        continue;
      }

      if (!item.integrityOk) {
        skip('integrity check failed');
        continue;
      }

      let parsed: unknown;
      try {
        parsed = JSON.parse(item.payload);
      } catch (e) {
        skip(`payload is not valid JSON: ${e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)}`);
        continue;
      }

      const validation = ContextSchema.safeParse(parsed);
      if (!validation.success) {
        skip(`payload failed schema validation: ${validation.error.issues[0]?.message ?? 'invalid'}`);
        continue;
      }

      const exists = await readFile(target, 'utf-8').then(
        () => true,
        () => false,
      );

      if (exists && !force) {
        skip('file exists (use force to overwrite)');
        continue;
      }

      if (exists) {
        await copyFile(target, `${target}.bak`);
      }

      const tmp = `${target}.tmp-${process.pid}-${Date.now()}`;
      try {
        await writeFile(tmp, item.payload, 'utf-8');
        await rename(tmp, target);
      } catch (e) {
        await unlink(tmp).catch(() => undefined);
        skip(`write failed: ${e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)}`);
        continue;
      }

      result.written.push(item.fileName);
    }

    return result;
  }
}

Note join is imported but the containment check uses resolve; drop the join import if tsc flags it as unused.

docs.title: Context sync to the memory service
docs.text: Design for issue #7. Status: approved, ready for an implementation plan.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Instincts sync to mcp-memory-service; contexts do not. CONTEXTS_PATH defaults to the directory shipped with the package, so a hand-authored context exists only on the machine that authored it. The v1.8 Python line could push contexts into memory and write them back on another machine; the TypeScript rewrite dropped both halves.

A memory stored on 2025-12-11 records the old behaviour: thirteen contexts tagged context-json,portable, stored in multiple parts, recreated through a create_context_file tool. Those memories still exist, so the port has real data to compare against.

docs.title: What was measured
docs.text:
Four facts settled the design. Each was measured against the running service, not assumed.

Storing a context as memory content does not round-trip. A 22,975-character context comes back as 4,976 characters. The service splits content over max_content_length into chunks and GET /memories/{hash} returns one of them.

Reassembling the service's own chunks cannot restore the original. split_content() is called with CONTENT_SPLIT_OVERLAP, so adjacent chunks share text. Concatenating them duplicates the overlap. Chunk metadata carries chunk_index, total_chunks and original_hash, so the siblings are findable — but findable is not the same as reassemblable.

Compressing into a single memory does not fit. The Cloudflare backend caps content at 800 characters, tied to the BGE model's 512-token limit. With the hybrid backend active that cap is binding. gzip+base64 of a 23 KB context is far above it.

Storing the file in metadata round-trips byte for byte. A 22,975-character payload in metadata.payload returned identical, as a single memory, with no chunking. This is the mechanism the design uses.

docs.title: Storage model
docs.text:
One memory per context.

  • content — a single readable line, Context <category>: <description>. This is what gets embedded, so a context stays findable by semantic search.
  • metadata.payload — the exact file text, byte for byte.
  • metadata — also file_name, context_version (from the context's own metadata.version), content_sha256 of the payload, source: mcp-context-provider, synced_at.
  • tags — context-json as the marker, context:<tool_category>, and portable for continuity with the v1 convention.

Metadata field names deliberately avoid chunk_index, total_chunks and original_hash: those belong to the service's own auto-splitting and must not be confused with ours.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
IMemoryBridge gains storeContext, listContexts and deleteContext. searchByTags is generalised to take the marker tag as a parameter instead of hard-coding instinctTag; the existing instinct methods become thin wrappers, so the instinct sync keeps working unchanged. MemoryBridgeConfig gains contextTag, defaulting to context-json.

ContextSync (src/bridge/context-sync.ts) mirrors InstinctSync.

  • pushToMemory(contexts) — per context: delete the existing memory found by context:<category>, then store fresh. Idempotent, the same shape as the instinct sync, so a re-push never duplicates.
  • pullFromMemory() — list the context-json memories and return payloads with their category, file name, version and SHA. Reading only; writing files is the caller's decision.

Engine gains syncContextsToMemory() and pullContextsFromMemory(), alongside the existing syncToMemory().

docs.title: What gets pushed
docs.text:
Everything the engine has loaded.

ContextLoader reads its base directory flat, with no recursion, so contexts/private/ is never loaded and therefore never pushed. The exclusion falls out of the existing architecture and needs no special case — but it is covered by a test, because it is now load-bearing for privacy rather than incidental.

For files that sit flat in contexts/ but should still stay local, a context may carry metadata.sync: false and is then skipped. The default is to sync. Two files in the working tree are the reason this exists: linkedin_context.json and n8n_context.json are gitignored yet loaded.

This matters because the memory service runs with MCP_MEMORY_STORAGE_BACKEND=hybrid: everything stored is replicated to Cloudflare D1 and Vectorize. A tag cannot prevent that — HybridStorage.store() enqueues every memory for replication without inspecting tags — so the decision of what leaves the machine has to be made here, before storing.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
sync_contexts — push. Reports pushed, skipped (with the reason: metadata.sync: false), and errors.

restore_contexts — pull and write into CONTEXTS_PATH. Writes only files that do not exist locally. An existing file is left untouched and reported as a conflict, showing the local and remote context_version. force: true overwrites, keeping a .bak of the previous file.

Never overwriting without force is a direct consequence of what happened in this repository: a store that was silently replaced lost 229 instincts, and the only reason they came back was a .bak left behind by something else.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
A context is skipped and reported, never written, when:

  • the payload's SHA-256 does not match content_sha256
  • the JSON fails ContextSchema validation
  • the target file exists and force is not set
  • file_name is not a plain basename matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*_context\.json$

That last rule exists because restore_contexts writes to a path derived from data held in the memory service. A file_name of ../../.ssh/authorized_keys must not be a way to write outside CONTEXTS_PATH, whatever put it there. The name is validated as a basename and the resolved target is checked to still sit inside CONTEXTS_PATH before anything is written.

Files are written atomically — temporary file, then rename — the same pattern InstinctLoader.save() uses since PR #6, so an interrupted write cannot leave a half-written context behind.

Bridge failures (unreachable service, auth failure) fail the whole operation with the HTTP status, rather than being recorded per context: if the bridge is down, every context would report the same error.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
A fake in-memory IMemoryBridge is introduced — none exists today, which is why InstinctSync has no unit tests either. It is written so the instinct sync can adopt it later.

  • push and pull round-trip a context byte for byte, including the largest real context in the repository
  • a re-push replaces rather than duplicates
  • a payload whose SHA does not match is rejected and not written
  • a payload that fails schema validation is rejected and not written
  • an existing local file is left byte-identical without force
  • with force, the file is replaced and a .bak holds the previous content
  • metadata.sync: false is not pushed
  • a context in a subdirectory of CONTEXTS_PATH is not pushed
  • a file_name containing a path separator or traversal segment is rejected and writes nothing

docs.title: Deliberately not in scope
docs.text:
• CLI commands. Instincts have mcp-cp; contexts are managed through the MCP tools for now. Adding a CLI surface is a separate change if it turns out to be wanted.
  • Reading the v1.8 memories. The old chunked context-json,portable entries use a different layout. They are left alone rather than migrated; the new format is written fresh.
  • Conflict merging. A conflict is reported, not resolved. Deciding which of two diverged contexts is right is a human judgement, and the version string is a free-form field with no ordering guarantee.

docs.title: Residual risk
docs.text: The metadata round-trip was measured against the local primary storage. That Cloudflare replication carries a 23 KB metadata blob was read from the code — json.dumps(memory.metadata) into a D1 column, with no length check or truncation — but not verified end to end. If it turns out D1 truncates, the fallback is deliberate chunking under our own context-part:i/n tags, which was the original plan before the metadata measurement.
